verdict.thesis_summary: Africell represents a premier frontier telecoms credit combining rapid market-share capture in Angola with sovereign risk mitigation from the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC). The credit has executed a remarkable deleveraging turnaround, reducing Net Leverage from 6.08x in FY24 to 3.52x in 2Q26 as 2Q26 Adj EBITDA surged +37.8% YoY to $40.5M (LTM $159.0M, +76.9% YoY). The 10.500% 2029 notes trade at 103.24 yielding 9.26% YTM (+452 bp spread), offering compelling high-coupon carry. Upside is bounded by the 23 October 2026 call date at 105.00 (8.76% YTW), creating an attractive short-duration defensive yield play with preferred creditor backing.

positives: High-Velocity Angola Commercial Growth: Broke the state-aligned Unitel/Movicel duopoly; active subscriber base surpassed 6M+ users, driving 2Q26 revenue up +16.1% YoY to $116.5M.

Strategic US Government (DFC) Backing: Direct debt partnership with the US International Development Finance Corporation provides powerful sovereign umbrella protection, FX repatriation facilitation, and geopolitical shielding under the Lobito Corridor initiative.

Dominant High-Margin Secondary Cash Cows: Market leadership in Sierra Leone (>60% share) and The Gambia (>60% share) delivers steady, predictable baseline cash flows that subsidize Angola's capex rollout.
Dramatic Post-Devaluation Deleveraging: Net leverage slashed by -2.56x from 6.08x in FY24 to 3.52x in 2Q26, driven by operational tariff adjustments and rapid subscriber density.
Clean, Transparent IFRS Reporting: Cognitive Credit audit confirms negligible management add-backs (Derived EBITDA of $158.8M vs Reported Adjusted EBITDA of $159.0M = 0.18% / $0.29M variance).
Healthy Interest Coverage Cushion: EBITDA interest coverage strengthened to 3.23x LTM, providing comfortable debt service headroom.
negatives: Free Cash Flow Burn: LTM FCF stands at -$62.5M due to aggressive network expansion capex ($68.0M LTM, $22.7M in 2Q26, 19.5% of sales) and working capital demands (-$59.3M LTM); however, 2Q26 FCF narrowed to -$4.7M.

Currency Mismatch & FX Conversion Risk: Tariffs collected in local currencies (Angolan Kwanza AOA, Congolese Franc CDF, Sierra Leonean Leone SLE, Gambian Dalasi GMD) against hard-currency USD debt service ($37.8M annual coupon on 2029 notes).

Tight Cash Buffer vs Near-Term Obligations: Cash and bank balances of $35.4M are closely matched against short-term term debt ($8.2M) and bank overdrafts ($29.7M), requiring continuous operational conversion.
Call Option Ceiling at 105.00: The notes become callable on 23 October 2026 at 105.00, capping capital appreciation potential above 105.

background.business_overview: Africell Holding Limited is an agile, private telecommunications operator providing voice, 4G/5G mobile broadband, and Afrimoney digital financial services across four high-growth Sub-Saharan African markets: Angola, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Sierra Leone, and The Gambia.
background.asset_perimeter: Nationwide cellular operating spectrum and concessions in Angola (Luanda, Benguela, Huambo, Lubango), DRC (Kinshasa, Katanga, Bas-Congo), Sierra Leone (Freetown and provinces), and The Gambia (Banjul), backed by extensive fiber-optic transmission and passive tower leases.
background.corporate_structure: Headquartered in London, UK. Owned by private holding vehicle (Lintel Group / Ziad Dalloul) with minority institutional and multilateral backing from the US DFC.

recent_drivers: 2Q26 Earnings Acceleration (18 Aug 2026): Revenue grew +16.1% YoY to $116.5M; Adjusted EBITDA jumped +37.8% YoY to $40.5M (margin 34.8%, +546 bps YoY); EBIT expanded +70.1% YoY to $21.0M (margin 18.0%).
Angola Network Reinvestment: Gross capex increased to $22.7M in 2Q26 (+101.8% YoY) as Africell deployed 4G LTE coverage across the central and southern provinces of Angola.
FCF Inflection: Free Cash Flow burn narrowed dramatically to -$4.7M in 2Q26 compared to -$43.5M in 1Q26, indicating approaching operating cash flow self-sufficiency.
Leverage Improvement: Total Net Debt ended 2Q26 at $560.4M, with Net Leverage falling to 3.52x, marking a continuous deleveraging trajectory from 6.08x in FY24.
